1	"""H1 gate audit (BRIEF H1) through the harness: what do the frozen ST7 (1 min) / ST8 (5 min) gates skip vs keep by
2	Foundation outcome? IS only; labels L1 (primary) and L0 (robustness).
3	
4	    python h1_gate_audit.py            # both timeframes, both labels; writes CSV / JSON / TABLES.md next to this file
5	
6	Definitions (fixed before any number was looked at):
7	  unit        a harness row: a Foundation SETUP taken under the label's book (harness.load(tf, label)); IS rows only
8	  kept        T.F.fz_traded: ST7/ST8 held a position on this SETUP (a TAKE, or a REENTER whose R5 was this SETUP). It is the
9	              frozen gate's kept set and is post-SETUP (the comparator, never a feature)
10	  gate_at     fz_gate (as of the SETUP bar); outcome_gate = fzpost_outcome_gate (post-SETUP: REENTER when a later REENTER
11	              used the SETUP as its R5)
12	  block_key   'BLOCK:<fz_block_reason>' when outcome_gate == BLOCK; 'WATCH:<fz_block_reason>' when outcome_gate == WATCH
13	              and a block reason is set (a refused TAKE branch that fell through to WATCH, e.g. leave_into_recycle);
14	              otherwise the outcome_gate itself (TAKE / REENTER / WATCH). Same definition as the local h1_common.py
15	  loser       label net <= 0 (costs included); winner = net > 0
16	  precision   P(loser | skipped); recall = P(skipped | loser); lift = precision / base loser rate (1.0 = random skipping)
17	  winner recall   count: P(kept | winner); |net|-weighted: kept winners' net / all winners' net
18	  big winner  label pts >= 50; huge >= 100 (the "late runners")
19	  pts bucket  (<=-50, (-50,-20], (-20,0], (0,20], (20,50], (50,100], >100); hold bucket (bars) 1-5, 6-15, 16-30, 31-60,
20	              61-120, 121-375, >375 on both timeframes (bars, not minutes)
21	  visit bin   fz_visit_n: 1 / 2 / 3 / 4+ / none (no ref room)
22	  variants    (all pre-declared; every one is a ledger row under family h1/<variant>)
23	              frozen                    keep = fz_traded
24	              take_only                 keep = fz_gate == TAKE (as of the bar)
25	              take_or_reenter_at_setup  keep = fz_gate in (TAKE, REENTER) (as of the bar)
26	              not_block                 keep = fzpost_outcome_gate != BLOCK (WATCH rows treated as taken; DIAGNOSTIC: uses a
27	                                        post column)
28	              skip_only:<block_key>     keep = block_key != key (skip only that key; DIAGNOSTIC: block_key uses the post
29	                                        outcome gate)
30	  FZ book     the ST7/ST8 position's own net on the kept rows (fzpos_l1_net_inr under L1, fzpos_net_inr under L0; REENTER
31	              fills a bar later and exits by its own rules, e.g. band_reclaim), Foundation's label net on the other rows;
32	              scored as label '<label>_fzpos' under family h1/fz_book. The selection-only book = frozen on the label itself
33	  bridge      Foundation IS net -> FZ book net = avoided price move of the skipped rows (-sum pts x 65) + avoided costs of
34	              the skipped rows (sum cost_inr = charges + 2 x 5 pts x 65 slippage) + REENTER exit delta (fzpos net - label net
35	              on kept rows). Cost avoidance is what any gate that trades less collects: reported, never counted as edge
36	  group tables  descriptive decompositions of the frozen ledger row by as-of and post columns (no rule is chosen on them)

114	def group_table(x, by):
115	    g = x.groupby(by, observed=True, dropna=False)

119	                          big=g.big.sum(), big_skipped=s.big.sum(), huge=g.huge.sum(), huge_skipped=s.huge.sum(),
120	                          kept_net=k.net.sum().round(2), skipped_net=s.net.sum().round(2), kept_mean=k.net.mean().round(2),
121	                          skipped_mean=s.net.mean().round(2), kept_win_rate=k.win.mean().round(4), skipped_win_rate=s.win.mean().round(4)))
122	    for c in ("kept_net", "skipped_net", "big_skipped", "huge_skipped"): t[c] = t[c].fillna(0)

127	def two_way(x, a, b):
128	    ct = x.pivot_table(index=a, columns=b, values="net", aggfunc=["count", "sum", "mean"], observed=True, fill_value=0)
129	    ct.columns = [f"{s}_{c}" for s, c in ct.columns]
130	    w = x.pivot_table(index=a, columns=b, values="win", aggfunc="sum", observed=True, fill_value=0)
131	    for c in w.columns: ct[f"winners_{c}"] = w[c]
132	    return ct.round(2).reset_index()

70	class Table:
71	    """One row per unit (a Foundation SETUP taken under the label's book), IS rows first in time order then OOS."""
72	
73	    def __init__(self, tf, label, F, TR, sessions):
74	        self.tf, self.label, self.F, self.TR, self.sessions = tf, label, F, TR, sessions
75	        self.n = len(F)
76	        self.setup_i = F.setup_i.to_numpy()
77	        self.entry_bar = self.setup_i
78	        self.session = F.session_idx.to_numpy()
79	        self.day = F.date.astype(str).to_numpy()
80	        self.is_mask = (F.split.astype(str) == "IS").to_numpy()
81	        self.oos_mask = ~self.is_mask
82	        pre = "l1_" if label == "L1" else "fnd_"
83	        self.net = F[pre + "net_inr"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
84	        self.pts = F[pre + "pts"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
85	        self.exit_bar = F[pre + "exit_i"].to_numpy(dtype=float).astype(int)
86	        self.win = self.net > 0
87	        self.entry_px = TR.entry_px.to_numpy(dtype=float); self.exit_px = TR[pre + "exit_px" if label == "L1" else "exit_px"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
88	        self.up = (F.dir.astype(str) == "up").to_numpy()
89	        self.net_slip = {s: self._net_at_slip(s) for s in (3.0, 5.0, 8.0)}
90	        assert np.allclose(self.net_slip[5.0], self.net, atol=0.02), "slippage 5 must reproduce the label's net"
91	        # 12 contiguous blocks of IS sessions (all IS sessions, active or not, so the blocks are time-contiguous)
92	        is_sess = sessions[sessions.split.astype(str) == "IS"].session_idx.to_numpy()
93	        edges = np.linspace(0, len(is_sess), N_BLOCKS + 1).round().astype(int)
94	        self.block_sessions = [is_sess[edges[b]:edges[b + 1]] for b in range(N_BLOCKS)]
95	        sess2block = {int(s): b for b in range(N_BLOCKS) for s in self.block_sessions[b]}
96	        self.block = np.array([sess2block.get(int(s), -1) for s in self.session])
97	        first_bar = dict(zip(sessions.session_idx, sessions.first_bar)); last_bar = dict(zip(sessions.session_idx, sessions.last_bar))
98	        self.block_range = [(int(first_bar[int(bs[0])]), int(last_bar[int(bs[-1])])) for bs in self.block_sessions]
99	        self.block_embargo = [set(int(s) for s in is_sess[edges[b + 1]:edges[b + 1] + EMBARGO_SESSIONS]) for b in range(N_BLOCKS)]
100	        self.active_sessions = np.array(sorted(set(self.session[self.is_mask].tolist())))
101	        self._asof = None
102	
103	    def _net_at_slip(self, s):
104	        out = np.empty(self.n)
105	        for i in range(self.n):
106	            e, x = self.entry_px[i], self.exit_px[i]
107	            if self.up[i]: buy, sell = e + s, x - s
108	            else: sell, buy = e - s, x + s
109	            out[i] = (sell - buy) * LOT - lab.trade_charges(CS, buy, sell, LOT)["total"]
110	        return out
111	
112	    def asof_columns(self):
113	        """Feature-eligible columns: every column that is not a label, a post-SETUP field, an identity or a raw price / id."""
114	        if self._asof is None:
115	            self._asof = [c for c in self.F.columns if not c.startswith(LABEL_PREFIX) and c not in NOT_FEATURES]
116	        return list(self._asof)
117	
118	    def with_label(self, name, net, exit_bar, pts=None):
119	        """A copy of the table under another label (L2 / L3 ...): net and exit bar per row; the splitter purges by exit_bar."""
120	        T = Table.__new__(Table); T.__dict__.update(self.__dict__)
121	        T.label, T.net, T.exit_bar = name, np.asarray(net, dtype=float), np.asarray(exit_bar).astype(int)
122	        T.pts = np.asarray(pts, dtype=float) if pts is not None else T.pts; T.win = T.net > 0
123	        T.net_slip = {s: self.net_slip[s] + (T.net - self.net) for s in self.net_slip}
124	        return T

139	def design(T, cols=None, max_levels=MAX_LEVELS):
140	    """Numeric design matrix over as-of columns: floats as they are (None -> NaN), booleans 0 / 1, text one-hot (<= max_levels
141	    levels, else dropped). Returns (X DataFrame, {encoded column: source column})."""
142	    cols = list(cols) if cols is not None else T.asof_columns()
143	    out, src = {}, {}
144	    for c in cols:
145	        s = T.F[c]
146	        if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s): out[c] = s.astype(float).to_numpy(); src[c] = c; continue
147	        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s): out[c] = s.to_numpy(dtype=float); src[c] = c; continue
148	        so = s.astype(object)
149	        vals = so.map(lambda z: None if z is None or (isinstance(z, float) and np.isnan(z)) else z)
150	        if all(isinstance(z, (bool, np.bool_)) or z is None for z in vals):
151	            out[c] = vals.map(lambda z: np.nan if z is None else float(z)).to_numpy(dtype=float); src[c] = c; continue
152	        levels = sorted({str(z) for z in vals if z is not None})
153	        if len(levels) > max_levels: continue
154	        for lv in levels:
155	            k = f"{c}={lv}"; out[k] = (vals.map(lambda z: None if z is None else str(z)) == lv).astype(float).to_numpy(); src[k] = c
156	    return pd.DataFrame(out), src

159	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the splitter
160	def _purge(T, train_idx, test_blocks):
161	    """Training rows whose label lifetime intersects a test block's bar range, or whose session is in its embargo, are dropped."""
162	    keep = np.ones(len(train_idx), dtype=bool)
163	    e0, e1 = T.entry_bar[train_idx], T.exit_bar[train_idx]
164	    ses = T.session[train_idx]
165	    for b in test_blocks:
166	        lo, hi = T.block_range[b]
167	        keep &= ~((e0 <= hi) & (e1 >= lo))
168	        keep &= ~np.isin(ses, list(T.block_embargo[b]))
169	    return train_idx[keep]
170	
171	
172	def purged_splits(T):
173	    """12 (train_idx, test_idx) over IS rows: test = one block; train = the other blocks, purged and embargoed."""
174	    is_idx = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
175	    for b in range(N_BLOCKS):
176	        te = is_idx[T.block[is_idx] == b]
177	        tr = _purge(T, is_idx[T.block[is_idx] != b], [b])
178	        yield tr, te
179	
180	
181	def cpcv_splits(T):
182	    """66 (train_idx, test_idx, (a, b)) with two test blocks each (N = 12, k = 2), purged against both and their embargoes."""
183	    is_idx = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
184	    for a, b in itertools.combinations(range(N_BLOCKS), CPCV_K):
185	        te = is_idx[np.isin(T.block[is_idx], [a, b])]
186	        tr = _purge(T, is_idx[~np.isin(T.block[is_idx], [a, b])], [a, b])
187	        yield tr, te, (a, b)

190	def cpcv_paths(T, oof_by_split):
191	    """11 backtest paths from the 66 CPCV splits. oof_by_split: {(a, b): array of decisions / scores for the rows of that
192	    split's test set, in the order cpcv_splits yields them}. Returns a list of 11 arrays over all rows (NaN outside IS): in
193	    path p, block g takes its prediction from the split that pairs g with its p-th other block."""
194	    is_idx = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
195	    paths = [np.full(T.n, np.nan) for _ in range(N_BLOCKS - 1)]
196	    for (a, b), pred in oof_by_split.items():
197	        te = is_idx[np.isin(T.block[is_idx], [a, b])]
198	        pred = np.asarray(pred, dtype=float); assert len(pred) == len(te), "prediction length must match the split's test rows"
199	        for g, other in ((a, b), (b, a)):
200	            p = [x for x in range(N_BLOCKS) if x != g].index(other)
201	            m = T.block[te] == g
202	            paths[p][te[m]] = pred[m]
203	    for p in paths: assert not np.isnan(p[is_idx]).any(), "every IS row must have a prediction in every path"
204	    return paths

207	def check_splits(T):
208	    """Leakage checks of the splitter: no training row's lifetime intersects its test block, no training row sits in the
209	    embargo, every IS row is tested once in the 12-block scheme; returns the counts."""
210	    n_te = np.zeros(T.n, dtype=int); purged = []
211	    for b, (tr, te) in enumerate(purged_splits(T)):
212	        lo, hi = T.block_range[b]
213	        assert not ((T.entry_bar[tr] <= hi) & (T.exit_bar[tr] >= lo)).any()
214	        assert not np.isin(T.session[tr], list(T.block_embargo[b])).any()
215	        assert (T.block[te] == b).all()
216	        n_te[te] += 1; purged.append(int(T.is_mask.sum() - len(te) - len(tr)))
217	    assert (n_te[T.is_mask] == 1).all() and (n_te[T.oos_mask] == 0).all()
218	    return dict(blocks=N_BLOCKS, rows_is=int(T.is_mask.sum()), rows_oos=int(T.oos_mask.sum()), purged_per_block=purged,
219	                block_sessions=[len(bs) for bs in T.block_sessions], block_rows=[int((T.block == b).sum()) for b in range(N_BLOCKS)],
220	                cpcv_splits=sum(1 for _ in cpcv_splits(T)))

238	def metrics(T, keep, rows, tag, controls=True, draws=CONTROL_DRAWS):
239	    """Kept-vs-skipped metrics of a boolean keep mask over the rows `rows` of T (a subset of one split)."""
240	    keep = np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)
241	    k = rows[keep[rows]]; s = rows[~keep[rows]]
242	    net, win = T.net, T.win
243	    nk, ns = len(k), len(s)
244	    m = dict(n=int(len(rows)), kept_n=int(nk), skipped_n=int(ns), kept_share=round(nk / len(rows), 4) if len(rows) else None,
245	             kept_net=round(float(net[k].sum()), 2), skipped_net=round(float(net[s].sum()), 2),
246	             kept_mean=round(float(net[k].mean()), 2) if nk else None, skipped_mean=round(float(net[s].mean()), 2) if ns else None,
247	             all_mean=round(float(net[rows].mean()), 2) if len(rows) else None,
248	             kept_win_rate=round(float(win[k].mean()), 4) if nk else None, skipped_win_rate=round(float(win[s].mean()), 4) if ns else None,
249	             kept_pf=None, kept_t=None, diff=None, diff_top1_removed=None, kept_mean_slip3=None, kept_mean_slip8=None,
250	             loser_recall=None, loser_precision=None, winner_recall=None, winner_recall_weighted=None, top_decile_winners_skipped=None,
251	             kept_sessions=int(len(set(T.session[k].tolist()))), sign_blocks=None, perm_p=None, control_pct=None, control_p_beat=None)
252	    if nk:
253	        w_, l_ = net[k][net[k] > 0], net[k][net[k] <= 0]
254	        m["kept_pf"] = round(float(w_.sum() / -l_.sum()), 3) if len(l_) and l_.sum() else None
255	        m["kept_t"] = round(float(net[k].mean() / (net[k].std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(nk))), 2) if nk > 1 and net[k].std(ddof=1) else None
256	    if nk and ns:
257	        m["diff"] = round(float(net[k].mean() - net[s].mean()), 2)
258	        # slippage moves every trade's net by the same amount, so the kept-vs-skipped difference is invariant; what a marginal
259	        # gate must survive is the kept book's own expectancy at 3 / 8 pts per side
260	        for sl_ in (3.0, 8.0): m[f"kept_mean_slip{int(sl_)}"] = round(float(T.net_slip[sl_][k].mean()), 2)
261	        top = np.quantile(net[rows], 0.99); kk, ss_ = k[net[k] < top], s[net[s] < top]
262	        m["diff_top1_removed"] = round(float(net[kk].mean() - net[ss_].mean()), 2) if len(kk) and len(ss_) else None
263	        L = ~win[rows]; W = win[rows]
264	        skp = ~keep[rows]
265	        m["loser_recall"] = round(float((skp & L).sum() / L.sum()), 4) if L.sum() else None
266	        m["loser_precision"] = round(float((skp & L).sum() / skp.sum()), 4) if skp.sum() else None
267	        m["winner_recall"] = round(float((~skp & W).sum() / W.sum()), 4) if W.sum() else None
268	        wn = net[rows]
269	        m["winner_recall_weighted"] = round(float(wn[~skp & W].sum() / wn[W].sum()), 4) if W.sum() and wn[W].sum() else None
270	        if W.sum():
271	            q = np.quantile(wn[W], 0.9); big = W & (wn >= q)
272	            m["top_decile_winners_skipped"] = round(float((skp & big).sum() / big.sum()), 4) if big.sum() else None
273	        bl = T.block[rows]
274	        if (bl >= 0).all():
275	            m["sign_blocks"] = int(sum(1 for b in range(N_BLOCKS) if (keep[rows] & (bl == b)).sum() and (~keep[rows] & (bl == b)).sum()
276	                                      and net[rows][keep[rows] & (bl == b)].mean() > net[rows][~keep[rows] & (bl == b)].mean()))
277	        if controls:
278	            pp = fz_report.permutation_p(net[k].tolist(), net[s].tolist(), draws, SEED, tag)
279	            m["perm_p"] = pp["p"]
280	            rc = fz_report.random_control(_units(T, rows), _units(T, k, "SEL"), draws, SEED, tag)
281	            m["control_pct"], m["control_p_beat"], m["control_p50"] = rc["fz_pct"], rc["p_beat"], rc["p50"]
282	    return m

285	def session_vectors(T, keep, rows):
286	    """Per active session (sessions with a unit among rows): kept sum / n, skipped sum / n, all sum / n."""
287	    keep = np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)
288	    ses = T.session[rows]; net = T.net[rows]; kp = keep[rows]
289	    S = np.array(sorted(set(ses.tolist())))
290	    idx = np.searchsorted(S, ses)
291	    out = {}
292	    for name, msk in (("kept", kp), ("skipped", ~kp), ("all", np.ones(len(rows), dtype=bool))):
293	        out[name + "_sum"] = np.bincount(idx, weights=net * msk, minlength=len(S))
294	        out[name + "_n"] = np.bincount(idx, weights=msk.astype(float), minlength=len(S))
295	    out["sessions"] = S
296	    return out

320	def score_paths(T, paths, family, config, script=None, controls=False, threshold=None):
321	    """CPCV: score each of the 11 path masks (a path is a decision array over rows: booleans, or scores compared with
322	    `threshold` when given). Returns the per-path metrics and the distribution of diff (median, 5th percentile, min) and of
323	    the control percentile when controls is set; every path is a ledger row of family '<family>/cpcv'."""
324	    out = []

328	    d = np.array([x["diff"] if x["diff"] is not None else np.nan for x in out], dtype=float)
329	    res = dict(paths=len(out), diff_median=round(float(np.nanmedian(d)), 2), diff_p5=round(float(np.nanquantile(d, 0.05)), 2),
330	               diff_min=round(float(np.nanmin(d)), 2), diff_share_positive=round(float((d > 0).mean()), 3),
331	               kept_share_median=round(float(np.median([x["kept_share"] for x in out])), 4))
332	    if controls:
333	        c = np.array([x["control_pct"] if x["control_pct"] is not None else np.nan for x in out], dtype=float)
334	        res.update(control_pct_median=round(float(np.nanmedian(c)), 1), control_pct_p5=round(float(np.nanquantile(c, 0.05)), 1))
335	    return res, out

358	def _partitions(S=CSCV_S):
359	    """All C(S, S/2) IS / pseudo-OOS block assignments as a boolean matrix (partitions x S), True = in-sample half."""
360	    combs = list(itertools.combinations(range(S), S // 2))

366	def pbo(vectors, statistic="kept_mean", S=CSCV_S):
367	    """CSCV probability of backtest overfitting (Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado & Zhu 2017) over a family of candidates.
368	    vectors: list of session_vectors dicts (one per candidate, same sessions). Each candidate's per-session series is split into
369	    S contiguous blocks; for every C(S, S/2) partition the IS-best candidate's OOS rank is recorded; PBO = share of partitions
370	    where that rank is below the median (logit < 0). statistic: 'kept_mean' = kept net per kept trade over the half, or 'diff'
371	    = kept mean minus skipped mean over the half. Also the IS-vs-OOS performance degradation slope and the share of partitions
372	    where the IS-best is below zero OOS."""
373	    M = len(vectors)
374	    if M < 2: return dict(candidates=M, pbo=None, note="needs at least 2 candidates")
375	    T_ = len(vectors[0]["sessions"]); edges = np.linspace(0, T_, S + 1).round().astype(int)
376	    def blocks(v, key):
377	        return np.array([v[key][edges[b]:edges[b + 1]].sum() for b in range(S)])
378	    KS = np.array([blocks(v, "kept_sum") for v in vectors]); KN = np.array([blocks(v, "kept_n") for v in vectors])
379	    SS = np.array([blocks(v, "skipped_sum") for v in vectors]); SN = np.array([blocks(v, "skipped_n") for v in vectors])
380	    P = _partitions(S).astype(float)                                           # partitions x S
381	    def perf(Pm):
382	        ks, kn = Pm @ KS.T, Pm @ KN.T                                           # partitions x M
383	        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
384	            km = np.where(kn > 0, ks / kn, np.nan)
385	            if statistic == "kept_mean": return km
386	            ss, sn = Pm @ SS.T, Pm @ SN.T
387	            return km - np.where(sn > 0, ss / sn, np.nan)
388	    ins, oos = perf(P), perf(1 - P)
389	    ins = np.where(np.isnan(ins), -np.inf, ins)
390	    best = np.argmax(ins, axis=1)
391	    oos_best = oos[np.arange(len(P)), best]
392	    ranks = np.array([(np.nan_to_num(oos[i], nan=-np.inf) < oos_best[i]).sum() / (M - 1) if M > 1 else 0.5 for i in range(len(P))])
393	    ranks = np.clip(ranks, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
394	    logit = np.log(ranks / (1 - ranks))
395	    ins_best = ins[np.arange(len(P)), best]
396	    ok = np.isfinite(oos_best) & np.isfinite(ins_best)
397	    slope = float(np.polyfit(ins_best[ok], oos_best[ok], 1)[0]) if ok.sum() > 2 else None
398	    return dict(candidates=M, partitions=int(len(P)), statistic=statistic, pbo=round(float((logit < 0).mean()), 4),
399	                oos_best_below_zero=round(float((oos_best[ok] < 0).mean()), 4) if ok.any() else None,
400	                degradation_slope=round(slope, 4) if slope is not None else None,
401	                is_best_mean=round(float(ins_best[ok].mean()), 2) if ok.any() else None,
402	                oos_best_mean=round(float(oos_best[ok].mean()), 2) if ok.any() else None)
403	
404	
405	def effective_trials(vectors, key="kept_sum"):
406	    """Participation-ratio count of independent trials from the correlation matrix of the candidates' per-session series."""
407	    X = np.array([v[key] for v in vectors], dtype=float)
408	    X = X[:, X.std(axis=0) > 0] if X.shape[0] > 1 else X
409	    if X.shape[0] < 2: return float(X.shape[0])
410	    C = np.corrcoef(X); C = np.nan_to_num(C, nan=0.0); np.fill_diagonal(C, 1.0)
411	    lam = np.clip(np.linalg.eigvalsh(C), 0, None)
412	    return round(float(lam.sum() ** 2 / (lam ** 2).sum()), 2)
413	
414	
415	def deflated_sharpe(per_session, n_trials, sr_var_trials=None):
416	    """Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014): the probability that the per-session Sharpe of a book is above the expected maximum
417	    Sharpe of n_trials trials with variance sr_var_trials (the variance of Sharpe across the family; estimated from
418	    per_session's own scale when None), with the skew / kurtosis correction. Returns SR, SR0, DSR, p = 1 - DSR."""
419	    x = np.asarray(per_session, dtype=float); T_ = len(x)
420	    if T_ < 3 or x.std(ddof=1) == 0: return dict(sr=None, sr0=None, dsr=None, p=None, T=T_)
421	    sr = float(x.mean() / x.std(ddof=1)); g3 = float(sst.skew(x)); g4 = float(sst.kurtosis(x, fisher=False))
422	    V = sr_var_trials if sr_var_trials is not None else 1.0 / T_
423	    N = max(2, n_trials); em = 0.5772156649
424	    sr0 = math.sqrt(V) * ((1 - em) * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / N) + em * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / (N * math.e)))
425	    den = 1 - g3 * sr + (g4 - 1) / 4 * sr * sr
426	    if den <= 0: return dict(sr=round(sr, 4), sr0=round(sr0, 4), dsr=None, p=None, T=T_, note="denominator <= 0")
427	    z = (sr - sr0) * math.sqrt(T_ - 1) / math.sqrt(den)
428	    dsr = float(sst.norm.cdf(z))
429	    return dict(sr=round(sr, 4), sr0=round(float(sr0), 4), dsr=round(dsr, 4), p=round(1 - dsr, 4), T=T_, n_trials=n_trials, skew=round(g3, 3), kurt=round(g4, 3))
430	
431	
432	def min_backtest_length(sr, n_trials, sr_var_trials):
433	    """Sessions needed for the observed per-session Sharpe to clear the expected maximum of n_trials (AFML 14.7)."""
434	    N = max(2, n_trials); em = 0.5772156649
435	    sr0 = math.sqrt(sr_var_trials) * ((1 - em) * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / N) + em * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / (N * math.e)))
436	    return round(float((sr0 / sr) ** 2 + 1), 1) if sr > 0 else None
437	
438	
439	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- resampling: stationary block bootstrap of sessions, SPA
440	def stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, mean_block=BOOT_MEAN_BLOCK, seed=SEED, tag=""):
441	    """Politis & Romano stationary bootstrap indices (draws x T_) over T_ ordered sessions; seeded and reproducible."""
442	    rng = np.random.default_rng(int(_sha(f"{seed}|boot|{tag}"), 16) % (2 ** 32))
443	    p = 1.0 / mean_block
444	    starts = rng.integers(0, T_, size=(draws, T_)); cont = rng.random((draws, T_)) >= p
445	    idx = np.empty((draws, T_), dtype=int)
446	    idx[:, 0] = starts[:, 0]
447	    for t_ in range(1, T_):
448	        idx[:, t_] = np.where(cont[:, t_], (idx[:, t_ - 1] + 1) % T_, starts[:, t_])
449	    return idx
450	
451	
452	def bootstrap_ci(vec, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, ci=GO["boot_ci"], tag=""):
453	    """Block-bootstrap CI (sessions resampled) of the kept-vs-skipped difference and of the kept mean from a session_vectors dict."""
454	    T_ = len(vec["sessions"]); idx = stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws, tag=tag)
455	    ks, kn, ss, sn = (vec[k][idx].sum(axis=1) for k in ("kept_sum", "kept_n", "skipped_sum", "skipped_n"))
456	    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
457	        km = np.where(kn > 0, ks / kn, np.nan); sm = np.where(sn > 0, ss / sn, np.nan); d = km - sm
458	    a = (1 - ci) / 2
459	    q = lambda v: [round(float(np.nanquantile(v, a)), 2), round(float(np.nanquantile(v, 1 - a)), 2)]
460	    return dict(draws=draws, ci=ci, diff_ci=q(d), kept_mean_ci=q(km), diff_p_le0=round(float(np.nanmean(d <= 0)), 4),
461	                diff_point=round(float(np.nansum(vec["kept_sum"]) / max(1, vec["kept_n"].sum()) - np.nansum(vec["skipped_sum"]) / max(1, vec["skipped_n"].sum())), 2))
462	
463	
464	def selection_gain(vec):
465	    """Per-session selection gain d_t = kept mean in session t minus the session's mean over all units (0 when nothing kept):
466	    the per-session statistic behind the session-matched random control (its expectation under random selection is 0)."""
467	    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
468	        km = np.where(vec["kept_n"] > 0, vec["kept_sum"] / vec["kept_n"], np.nan)
469	        am = vec["all_sum"] / vec["all_n"]
470	    d = km - am
471	    return np.where(np.isnan(d), 0.0, d), vec["kept_n"] > 0
472	
473	
474	def spa(vectors, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, tag="", min_active=None):
475	    """White's Reality Check and Hansen's SPA over a family of candidates: H0 = no candidate has positive expected selection
476	    gain (per-session kept mean minus the session mean). Stationary bootstrap of sessions, Hansen's consistent recentring;
477	    reported both studentised (Hansen) and unstudentised (White's original statistic, sqrt(T) x mean). A candidate whose
478	    selection gain differs from zero in fewer than `min_active` sessions (default max(10, 5% of T)) is excluded from the
479	    studentised family: its near-zero variance would give it an arbitrarily large t (the exit-policy refuter's finding); it
480	    stays in the unstudentised family. Returns the best candidate under each statistic and the four p-values."""
481	    Dm = np.array([selection_gain(v)[0] for v in vectors], dtype=float)       # M x T
482	    M, T_ = Dm.shape
483	    if min_active is None: min_active = max(10, int(0.05 * T_))
484	    active = (np.abs(Dm) > 1e-9).sum(axis=1)
485	    ok = active >= min_active
486	    mu = Dm.mean(axis=1); sd = Dm.std(axis=1, ddof=1) + 1e-12
487	    idx = stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws, tag=tag)
488	    mub = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].mean(axis=1) for d in range(draws)])           # draws x M
489	    sdb = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].std(axis=1, ddof=1) for d in range(draws)]) + 1e-12
490	    thr = np.sqrt(np.var(Dm, axis=1, ddof=1) / T_ * 2 * math.log(math.log(T_)))
491	    mu_c = np.where(mu < -thr, mu, 0.0)                                            # Hansen's consistent recentring
492	    out = dict(candidates=M, sessions=T_, draws=draws, min_active_sessions=int(min_active), excluded_from_studentised=int((~ok).sum()))
493	    # unstudentised (White 2000): statistic sqrt(T) x mean gain, every candidate
494	    tu = np.sqrt(T_) * mu; bu = int(np.argmax(tu)); stat_u = float(tu[bu])
495	    rc_u = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu), axis=1); spa_u = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu + mu_c), axis=1)
496	    out.update(best_unstudentised=bu, best_mean_gain_unstudentised=round(float(mu[bu]), 2),
497	               rc_p_unstudentised=round(float((rc_u >= stat_u).mean()), 4), spa_p_unstudentised=round(float((spa_u >= stat_u).mean()), 4))
498	    # studentised (Hansen 2005), candidates with enough active sessions
499	    if ok.any():
500	        ts = np.where(ok, np.sqrt(T_) * mu / sd, -np.inf); bs = int(np.argmax(ts)); stat_s = float(ts[bs])
501	        rc_s = np.max(np.where(ok, np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu) / sdb, -np.inf), axis=1)
502	        spa_s = np.max(np.where(ok, np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu + mu_c) / sdb, -np.inf), axis=1)
503	        out.update(best=bs, best_mean_gain=round(float(mu[bs]), 2), best_t=round(stat_s, 3), best_active_sessions=int(active[bs]),
504	                   rc_p=round(float((rc_s >= stat_s).mean()), 4), spa_p=round(float((spa_s >= stat_s).mean()), 4))
505	    else:
506	        out.update(best=None, best_mean_gain=None, best_t=None, best_active_sessions=None, rc_p=None, spa_p=None)
507	    return out
508	
509	
510	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- structural breaks of the book's own expectancy
511	def _hac_var(x, lag=5):
512	    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float) - np.mean(x); T_ = len(x)
513	    s = float((x * x).sum())
514	    for k in range(1, lag + 1):
515	        w = 1 - k / (lag + 1); s += 2 * w * float((x[k:] * x[:-k]).sum())
516	    return s / T_ / T_                                                             # variance of the mean
517	
518	
519	def chow_mean(x, y, lag=5):
520	    """HAC (Newey-West, Bartlett, lag 5) t-test of a difference of means between two consecutive segments."""
521	    x, y = np.asarray(x, dtype=float), np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
522	    if len(x) < 5 or len(y) < 5: return dict(t=None, p=None, n=[len(x), len(y)])
523	    t_ = (y.mean() - x.mean()) / math.sqrt(_hac_var(x, lag) + _hac_var(y, lag))
524	    return dict(t=round(float(t_), 3), p=round(float(2 * (1 - sst.norm.cdf(abs(t_)))), 4), mean_before=round(float(x.mean()), 2),
525	                mean_after=round(float(y.mean()), 2), n=[len(x), len(y)])
526	
527	
528	def bde_cusum(x, k=10):
529	    """Brown-Durbin-Evans CUSUM of recursive residuals of the constant-mean model on the ordered series x: the maximum
530	    crossing of the 5% bands +-0.948 sqrt(T-k) (1 + 2 (r-k)/(T-k)); reports whether the path leaves the band and where."""
531	    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float); T_ = len(x)
532	    if T_ <= k + 2: return dict(break_detected=None)
533	    w = np.array([(x[t_] - x[:t_].mean()) / math.sqrt(1 + 1 / t_) for t_ in range(k, T_)])
534	    sig = w.std(ddof=1)
535	    W = np.cumsum(w) / sig
536	    r = np.arange(k + 1, T_ + 1)
537	    band = 0.948 * math.sqrt(T_ - k) * (1 + 2 * (r - k) / (T_ - k))
538	    ex = np.abs(W) > band
539	    return dict(break_detected=bool(ex.any()), first_crossing_index=int(np.argmax(ex)) + k if ex.any() else None,
540	                max_ratio=round(float(np.max(np.abs(W) / band)), 3), T=T_)
541	
542	
543	def break_tests(T, lag=5):
544	    """The pre-registration step: has the book's per-session expectancy (active sessions, label L1) changed inside IS or at the
545	    IS / OOS boundary? Rolling 60-session mean with block-bootstrap bands, BDE CUSUM, HAC Chow tests per calendar year, and the
546	    one permitted OOS aggregate read: the Chow test at 2026-01-01 (it decides the OOS caveat, never a key)."""
547	    rows = np.arange(T.n)
548	    ses = T.session[rows]; net = T.net[rows]
549	    S = np.array(sorted(set(ses.tolist()))); idx = np.searchsorted(S, ses)
550	    per = np.bincount(idx, weights=net, minlength=len(S)) / np.bincount(idx, minlength=len(S))
551	    day = dict(zip(T.session, T.day)); days = np.array([day[int(s)] for s in S])
552	    is_ = days <= IS_END
553	    x_is = per[is_]
554	    years = sorted({d[:4] for d in days[is_]})
555	    chow_years = {}
556	    for y in years[1:]:
557	        before = x_is[np.array([d[:4] < y for d in days[is_]])]; after = x_is[np.array([d[:4] == y for d in days[is_]])]
558	        chow_years[y] = chow_mean(before, after, lag)
559	    boundary = chow_mean(x_is, per[~is_], lag)
560	    roll = pd.Series(x_is).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy()
561	    idxb = stationary_bootstrap_idx(len(x_is), 500, tag="roll")
562	    rb = np.array([pd.Series(x_is[idxb[d]]).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy() for d in range(500)])
563	    lo, hi = np.nanquantile(rb, 0.05, axis=0), np.nanquantile(rb, 0.95, axis=0)
564	    outside = int(np.nansum((roll < lo) | (roll > hi)))
565	    return dict(label=T.label, active_is_sessions=int(is_.sum()), is_mean_per_session=round(float(x_is.mean()), 2),
566	                bde=bde_cusum(x_is), chow_per_year=chow_years, chow_is_oos_boundary=boundary,
567	                rolling60_outside_band=outside, rolling60_points=int(np.isfinite(roll).sum()),
568	                winners_only_boundary=chow_mean(x_is[x_is > 0], per[~is_][per[~is_] > 0], lag) if (per[~is_] > 0).sum() >= 5 else None,
569	                caveat=("IS/OOS boundary Chow p < 0.05: the OOS window is not from the same process; every OOS table carries this"
570	                        if boundary["p"] is not None and boundary["p"] < 0.05 else "no boundary break at 5%"))
571	
572	
573	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- go / no-go
574	def go_no_go(res, tf, cpcv=None, pbo_value=None, dsr=None, spa_p=None, boot=None):
575	    """The pre-registered pass rule on a candidate's IS results. Returns (passed, {check: (ok, value)})."""
576	    ch = {}
577	    ch["kept_share>=20%"] = (res.get("kept_share") is not None and res["kept_share"] >= GO["kept_share_min"], res.get("kept_share"))
578	    ch[f"kept_n>={GO['kept_n_min'][tf]}"] = (res.get("kept_n", 0) >= GO["kept_n_min"][tf], res.get("kept_n"))
579	    ch["diff>0"] = (res.get("diff") is not None and res["diff"] > 0, res.get("diff"))
580	    ch["diff_top1_removed>0"] = (res.get("diff_top1_removed") is not None and res["diff_top1_removed"] > GO["top1_removed_diff_min"], res.get("diff_top1_removed"))
581	    ch["kept_mean_slip8>0"] = (res.get("kept_mean_slip8") is not None and res["kept_mean_slip8"] > GO["slip8_kept_mean_min"], res.get("kept_mean_slip8"))
582	    ch[f"sign_blocks>={GO['sign_blocks_min']}/12"] = (res.get("sign_blocks") is not None and res["sign_blocks"] >= GO["sign_blocks_min"], res.get("sign_blocks"))
583	    ch["control_pct>=95"] = (res.get("control_pct") is not None and res["control_pct"] >= GO["control_pct_min"], res.get("control_pct"))
584	    if cpcv is not None: ch["cpcv_p5_diff>0"] = (cpcv.get("diff_p5") is not None and cpcv["diff_p5"] > GO["cpcv_p5_diff_min"], cpcv.get("diff_p5"))
585	    if pbo_value is not None: ch["pbo<=0.2"] = (pbo_value <= GO["pbo_max"], pbo_value)
586	    if dsr is not None: ch["dsr_p<0.1"] = (dsr.get("p") is not None and dsr["p"] < GO["dsr_p_max"], dsr.get("p"))
587	    if spa_p is not None: ch["spa_p<=0.10"] = (spa_p <= GO["spa_p_max"], spa_p)
588	    if boot is not None: ch["boot_ci_excludes_0"] = (boot["diff_ci"][0] > 0, boot["diff_ci"])
589	    return all(v[0] for v in ch.values()), ch
590	
591	
592	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- self-test
593	if __name__ == "__main__":
594	    import argparse, time
595	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument("--tf", default="5minute"); ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true"); a = ap.parse_args()
596	    t0 = time.time()
597	    T = load(a.tf)
598	    print(f"{a.tf} L1 units: {T.n} (IS {T.is_mask.sum()}, OOS {T.oos_mask.sum()}), as-of columns {len(T.asof_columns())}, active IS sessions {len(T.active_sessions)}")
599	    print("splits:", json.dumps(check_splits(T)))
600	    X, src = design(T); print(f"design matrix {X.shape}, NaN share {X.isna().mean().mean():.3f}")
601	    frozen = T.F.fz_traded.astype(bool).to_numpy()
602	    r1 = score(T, frozen, "selftest/frozen_gate", dict(gate="ST7/ST8 as traded"), script=__file__)
603	    print("frozen gate:", {k: r1[k] for k in ("kept_n", "kept_share", "kept_mean", "skipped_mean", "diff", "perm_p", "control_pct", "loser_recall", "winner_recall_weighted", "sign_blocks", "kept_mean_slip8")})
604	    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
605	    vecs = [session_vectors(T, frozen, np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask))]
606	    for j in range(5):
607	        kp = rng.random(T.n) < 0.5
608	        score(T, kp, "selftest/random", dict(seed=j), script=__file__, controls=False)
609	        vecs.append(session_vectors(T, kp, np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)))
610	    print("pbo (kept_mean):", pbo(vecs, "kept_mean")); print("pbo (diff):", pbo(vecs, "diff"))
611	    print("effective trials:", effective_trials(vecs))
612	    gain, _ = selection_gain(vecs[0])
613	    print("dsr (frozen, per-session kept net, 6 trials):", deflated_sharpe(np.where(vecs[0]["kept_n"] > 0, vecs[0]["kept_sum"] / np.maximum(vecs[0]["kept_n"], 1), 0.0)[vecs[0]["kept_n"] > 0], 6, 0.01))
614	    print("bootstrap:", bootstrap_ci(vecs[0], draws=500))
615	    print("spa:", spa(vecs, draws=500))
616	    print("break tests:", json.dumps(break_tests(T), default=str)[:1500])
617	    print("go/no-go frozen:", go_no_go(r1, a.tf))
618	    print(f"self-test done in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s; ledger sha {ledger_sha()}")

1	# FZ v3 design panel (2026-09-29)
2	
3	Three designers (quant-ML canon, sequence / representation learning, decision-making / RL) proposed studies for the FZ v3 program; two judges (feasibility-and-rigour, skeptical practitioner) scored each on feasible_here / rigour / expected_value (0-5) with keep = all three >= 3. Generated from the workflow result; the judges' fixes are part of the program. Feasibility was scored against the local 4-core box; in the cloud the compute ceilings do not apply, the rigour and overfitting fixes do.
4	
5	## Scoreboard
6	
7	| id | lens priority | J1 feas/rig/ev keep | J2 feas/rig/ev keep |
8	|---|---|---|---|
9	| deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses | 1 | 5/3/3 KEEP | 5/3/3 KEEP |
10	| deep-sequence-regime-states | 2 | 4/4/2 drop | 4/4/3 KEEP |
11	| deep-sequence-rocket-probe | 3 | 3/3/2 drop | 3/4/2 drop |
12	| deep-sequence-vision-labels | 4 | 3/3/2 drop | 3/3/3 KEEP |
13	| deep-sequence-motif-shapelet | 5 | 4/3/1 drop | 4/4/2 drop |
14	| deep-sequence-pretrain-probe | 6 | 2/3/1 drop | 2/4/1 drop |
15	| quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo | 1 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/5/4 KEEP |
16	| quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate | 2 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/4/4 KEEP |
17	| quant-ml-canon-feature-importance | 3 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/4/3 KEEP |
18	| quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip | 4 | 5/4/2 drop | 5/4/3 KEEP |
19	| quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing | 5 | 5/3/2 drop | 5/4/2 drop |
20	| quant-ml-canon-regime-breaks | 6 | 4/4/2 drop | 5/4/3 KEEP |
21	| decision-making-1-fullinfo-bandit-policy-tree-gate | 1 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/4/4 KEEP |
22	| decision-making-2-exit-policy-fqi-exomdp | 2 | 2/4/3 drop | 3/4/3 KEEP |
23	| decision-making-3-robustness-resampling-multiplicity-adversarial | 3 | 4/4/3 KEEP | 3/4/3 KEEP |
24	| decision-making-4-selective-gate-conformal-risk-control | 4 | 5/4/2 drop | 5/4/3 KEEP |
25	| decision-making-5-kelly-bounded-sizing | 5 | 5/3/1 drop | 5/4/2 drop |
26	| decision-making-6-session-stop-rule-finite-horizon | 6 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/5/3 KEEP |
27	
28	## Judges' verdicts
29	
30	### Judge 1
31	
32	Skeptical-practitioner verdict. The tape sets the ceiling before any model runs: 1m Foundation is +1.9 pts per trade gross against ~16 pts of cost (mean net -922 INR, 15.2% winners, 4,502 IS SETUPs in 579 active sessions); 5m is 184 IS winners with the top decile carrying ~46% of gross and an IS-to-OOS mean shift from -277 to -1,060 per trade. So any gate must find a subset whose expectancy clears ~16-20 pts, and the whole signal lives in a few hundred trades on 1m and a few dozen on 5m. On that sample the block-bootstrap CI of a kept-vs-skipped difference will be several hundred INR per trade wide; most candidates will not clear it, and that is the honest expected outcome. Every library the 18 studies name is present (sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib) and statsmodels/torch/mapie are absent as assumed; feasibility failures are compute and memory, not imports.
33	
34	Keep seven, merged into five lines of work, about 1-1.5 CPU-hours per timeframe in total: (1) one validation harness = quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's SPA, adversarial drift and 5m null tapes folded in (one ledger, one bootstrap, one PBO, active sessions only, every comparator re-priced on the L1 15:25 label); (2) one feature-vocabulary pass = quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, its 8-cluster shortlist frozen in the ledger before any gate search, with BOCPD, FFD and the novelty scalars entering there and nowhere else; (3) one learned-gate family = quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate and decision-making-1 merged (L1 label, capped |net| weights, top-1%-winners-removed as a hard pass, block-wise sign test, one distilled rule list or scorecard as the single OOS candidate from the family); (4) the interpretable candidate = deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses with a blind round 0 from the user's words alone, hashed before any table is shown, and cross-fitted round-1 tables; (5) the cheap desk rule = decision-making-6 session stop with an hour-conditioned null. That yields at most three OOS looks: the rule list from (3), the round-0 list from (4), and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator, with (5) as a multiplication if its null is rejected.
35	
36	Drop or defer eleven. The sequence and representation studies (rocket, pretrain, HMM/jump, motif/shapelet, vision) share one structural flaw: the only shippable form is a depth-3 tree on the same scalar features the tabular studies already search, so they add trials to the ledger without adding a candidate, and the pre-SETUP window is templated by the engine's own SETUP definition; pretrain and 1m FQI also need 750-900 MB for hours on a box shared with another build. The two conformal studies and the two sizing studies do not change which SETUPs are taken: they choose a threshold on a score another study produces, or size a positive edge that does not yet exist; their useful pieces (slippage 3/5/8 sensitivity, Pareto front with user-chosen w, |net|-weighted coverage, one-lot-or-skip verdict) become sections of the gate study's deliverable. The regime-breaks study keeps only its break tests as the harness's pre-registration step (they decide time-decay weights and the OOS caveat); BSADF is a feature candidate for the importance pass, not a gate. The exit study is worth its parametric learner C (config keys the lab already has, 10 minutes by replay) but must be coordinated with the ST9-12 session, which already ran an exit grid on 2026.
37	
38	Two standing caveats every OOS table must carry: the OOS window (2026-01-01..09-25) is also the published lab dashboard window and was used by the ST9-12 exit grid, so it is not pristine; and the 5m Foundation label as built holds 358 of 1,012 trades past the entry session, so ST13/ST14 (square_off 15:25) must be judged on the recomputed intraday label and every comparator re-priced on it.
39	
40	### Judge 2
41	
42	Twelve of eighteen studies are worth running here; six are cut or folded. The binding facts: (1) sample size, not compute, is the limit: 684 IS winners on 1m and 184 on 5m, a 15-22% win rate, mean net -922 INR per trade against ~1,050 INR costs, so a gate must find a subset averaging > 16 pts, and the top-decile winners are half of gross wins; every learned number must therefore be reported as a CPCV path distribution (5th percentile), with |net| weights winsorised and kept-n floors. (2) memory: lab.py holds 1.24 GB and 759 MB is free, so the '2 processes under 1 GB' budget is currently one process under ~600 MB; the rocket probe at 10k kernels, the pretrain ladder, 1m FQI and 1m synthetic tapes do not fit until lab.py exits. (3) libraries: everything named that is present imports (numpy, pandas, scipy, sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, matplotlib, PIL, joblib); statsmodels, torch, mapie, hmmlearn, ruptures, arch are absent and every study that names them correctly hand-codes. Structural fixes that apply across the set: there must be ONE harness (merge quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's bootstrap/PBO): 12 contiguous IS session blocks, purge by the label's own exit bar, 3-session embargo, one append-only ledger reached only through a score() function, PBO <= 0.2, kept-share/kept-n floors, slippage-8-pt survival, and ONE OOS script run once for at most 3 frozen candidates; all eighteen 'OOS once' clauses collapse into that, otherwise OOS is opened eighteen times. Four near-duplicate pairs merge: meta-label + policy-tree gate (the central study, EV 4), conformal-skip + conformal-risk-control (one operating-point step the user chooses on), the two sizing studies (conditional on a gate surviving; prior is 'one lot or skip'), the two harnesses. The L1 intraday (15:25) label written once is the only training label; the engine label's multi-session holds (358 of 1,012 on 5m) make purging by it too costly. Regime, novelty and state-model outputs enter as candidate features into the importance study rather than as separate gate searches, which is the cheapest cut in multiplicity. The LLM-hypothesis study needs a blind round 0 and a trials count equal to the labelled cells shown; the vision study runs as a 40-session pilot against mechanical proxies first; both must be separate agents from any study author. Cut: pretrain-probe (3-4 h, 750 MB, negative result foreseen), motif/shapelet (keep only the causal novelty score), rocket as proposed (reduce to a 5-minute ceiling check), both sizing studies as standalone. Run order: break tests and L1 label, harness, importance, merged gate, operating point, exit learners C and B (FQI on 5m only), session-stop, BOCPD/GMM regime, LLM rounds, vision pilot, null tapes on 5m; everything above 600 MB waits for lab.py.
43	
44	## Designers' rationales
45	
46	- What this lens can honestly do on this box. The brief's data now exists in the session scratchpad (fz_v3/5minute complete; fz_v3/minute engine/trades written, features running): 5m has 1,012 Foundation SETUPs (832 IS / 180 OOS, 22% net winners, mean net -277 INR), 1m has 5,326 (4,502 IS / 824 OOS, 15% winners, mean net -922 INR, sd ~5,300 INR, median hold 15 bars, p90 92). So the supervised sample is 4.5k rows with ~680 positive labels on 1m and 830 rows with 184 positives on 5m; OOS confirmation rests on 128 and 37 winners respectively. Standard error of an OOS mean net is ~185 INR/trade (1m) and ~375 INR/trade (5m): a gate must move kept-vs-skipped expectancy by roughly 500 (1m) / 1,000 (5m) INR per trade to be visible at all, and nothing subtler is decidable on this tape. Every study below is sized to that reality: the models are feature extractors and regime detectors whose output is distilled into a compact rule list, not end-to-end deep classifiers.
47	
48	Library reality, checked with `python -c import`: torch, tensorflow, hmmlearn, stumpy, ruptures, tslearn, sktime, pyts are absent and nothing may be installed. Present: numpy 2.2, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3, scipy 1.14, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2, shap 0.49, matplotlib 3.9, PIL, pyarrow, psutil. Consequences, stated per study: a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer is not possible without a framework (a hand-written numpy CNN is a day of build for no expected gain at n=4.5k); its honest modern substitute is the random-convolutional-kernel transform (ROCKET/MiniRocket) plus a linear probe, which the literature shows matches small CNNs on small time-series benchmarks and which I benchmarked here at 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels. Contrastive pretraining (InfoNCE) needs a custom loss, so the self-supervised study uses the ladder PCA -> sklearn MLP autoencoder -> forecast-pretext encoder and reports whether anything beats PCA. Matrix profile, HMM, statistical jump model and Bayesian online change-point detection are all implementable in numpy/numba in under 150 lines each and were timed (FFT distance profile 0.19 s per query over the whole 445k-bar 1m tape; GMM on 90k x 6 in 51 s).
49	
50	Machine: 4 cores, 7.9 GB total but only ~0.9 GB free at the time of writing (lab.py rebuild holds 1.5 GB, the 1m feature build ~200 MB), so studies must run one at a time until the rebuild finishes, and every study is designed to peak under 800 MB with 1m windows stored as float32 and never more than ~150k pretraining windows in memory at once.
51	
52	Common protocol shared by all six (each study's leakage_controls field adds the study-specific parts): (1) unit = Foundation SETUP with its own engine trade from the build (fnd_net_inr, fnd_win, exit reason); (2) every feature/window uses bars <= setup_i (the SETUP bar's close is the entry; the window ends at k inclusive); (3) IS-only learning with purged, embargoed, session-blocked CV: 5 contiguous chronological blocks of ~205 IS sessions, training SETUPs whose Foundation exit session falls in the test block or its embargo are purged, embargo = max sessions_held observed on that timeframe (+1), all normalisation/PCA/kernel-bias/model parameters fit inside the training folds; (4) OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) is scored once by a single logged script run with the model frozen on all IS, never re-tuned; (5) judgement is kept-vs-skipped mean-net difference with fz_report.permutation_p, the session-matched random control percentile (fz_report.random_control; the current ST7/ST8 sit at the 39.6th/57th percentile, so the bar is 'above the 95th'), precision/recall on losers, and the share of top-decile winners skipped; net alone is never the criterion because every gate that trades less banks ~1,114 INR per skipped 1m trade; (6) multiplicity: every configuration tried is counted and a max-T permutation across the family (White's Reality Check style) is reported next to the single-rule p; (7) output = a candidate ST13/ST14 gate block: <= 8 conjunctive rules of depth <= 3 over named as-of features with provenance 'learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script <name>, sha'; any non-scalar artefact (HMM parameters, a shapelet template) is offered only as an alternative that needs a user decision on a new fz key and code contract.
53	
54	Ordering: the LLM-hypothesis study is first because it is config-native, cheap and directly encodes the user's own reads; the regime-state study second because 'sideways hurts' is the user's central claim and the models are small enough to ship; the random-kernel probe third as the cheapest ceiling test for 'is there information in the bar shape at all'; vision labels fourth because they give the user's visual notion of sideways a ground truth (and the first number, Foundation expectancy by hindsight label, decides whether any causal detector is worth building); motif/shapelet fifth; self-supervised pretraining last because without a framework it is the most likely to report 'nothing beyond PCA'. Sizing and exits: studies 2 and 3 emit a per-SETUP expectancy score; the brief's exits stay Foundation's, so sizing appears only as a secondary output (lots 0/1/2 by score tercile) judged with the same control; a during-trade version of the window models for early exits is a natural follow-on once the position-path table exists, and is not proposed here.
55	
56	- Lens and framing. Foundation is the primary model: it fixes side, entry bar and exit rule for every SETUP, and (decisively) its outcome is observed for every SETUP in the data, taken or not. So the take/skip/size decision at the SETUP bar is a one-step problem with full-information feedback: it is supervised meta-labelling in Lopez de Prado's sense, not a bandit (no off-policy correction is needed because the counterfactual is in the table) and not sequential RL (no position overlap: 0 of 1,003 Foundation trades overlap on 5m, by construction the next SETUP needs the CHoCH that exits the previous trade). Everything proposed below descends from that framing: the labels and weights (AFML ch. 3-4), the validation harness (ch. 7, 11-14), importance with substitution effects removed (ch. 8; MLAM ch. 6), calibrated sizing (ch. 10), conformal sets for the skip decision (Vovk; Angelopoulos and Bates), and break/explosiveness statistics as regime features (ch. 17). Sample-size reality drives the design: on 5m IS there are 823 SETUPs and 181 winners; the engine-label net has std 10,271 INR (holds run to 70 sessions because the engine has no square-off), so a kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference below about 1,400 INR per trade (400 vs 400 split, 5% two-sided) is undetectable on that label. The intraday label (exit forced at the entry session's 15:25 bar, the lab's ST1/ST2 book) is therefore the primary label in every study; the top decile of winners carries 46% of gross wins (win mean +10,878, loss mean -3,429), so every gate is judged on |net|-weighted winner recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy plus the session-matched random control, never on accuracy or net alone (a gate that trades less always saves costs). Data facts the studies rely on: the 5-minute table at scratchpad/fz_v3/5minute (features.parquet, 186 columns, 143 as-of; 97 numeric with 114 pairs |rho| > 0.9; causality verified by the truncated build), the 1-minute table not yet landed (scripts 01-03 only) but promised with the same column contract (a few thousand SETUPs). Box: 4 logical cores, 7.9 GB RAM with about 1.2 GB free beside the other session's 1.1 GB lab process; every study is a single process under 500 MB and 25 CPU-minutes per timeframe, at most two at a time, no pip installs (numpy 2.2.6, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.14.1, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, numba 0.65, joblib; statsmodels/mapie/mlfinlab/lightgbm/torch absent, so ADF, CUSUM, FFD, conformal and PBO are hand-coded in numpy, all short). Order and dependencies: the harness (study 2) first because every other study and H1-H5 consume its splitter and trials ledger; then meta-labelling (1) which also hands H5 its labels, weights, OOF probabilities and splitter instead of a second gradient-boosting run; importance (3) and regime (6) can run in parallel with (1) since they only need the splitter; conformal (4) and sizing (5) consume (1)'s OOF file and are cheap. Deliberately left out with reasons: sequential bootstrap (uniqueness is 1 by construction for Foundation labels; only the triple-barrier variants with vertical barriers overlap and those get the concurrency weights inside study 1); HRP / portfolio construction (one instrument); deep sequence models and transformers (1k-5k labels, no GPU, and nothing to distil into 8 rules); sequential RL (one-step decision with the counterfactual observed); generative AI in the LLM sense (no standing in the canon at this sample size; the only generative element the canon endorses here is the CPCV path distribution and the stationary block bootstrap of sessions in study 2, which is what gives the confidence intervals). OOS discipline shared by all six: candidate configs and the exact scoring scripts are frozen to JSON with a sha before any OOS row is read; the harness pre-registers the go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV 5th-percentile kept-vs-skipped difference > 0, deflated-Sharpe p < 0.1, at most three candidates across all lenses get the one OOS look); the frozen ST7/ST8 gate is always one of the comparators; ST13/ST14 must carry square_off "15:25" so that the traded book matches the label the gate was learned on.
57	
58	- Why this lens splits the problem the way it does. (1) The take/skip choice at a Foundation SETUP is a contextual bandit with FULL information: Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of "take" (fnd_net, 1m: 5,326 rows, 5m: 1,012 rows) is logged for every context, and the reward of "skip" is exactly 0 by definition. There is no unobserved arm, hence no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction: the off-policy value of ANY gate pi is computed exactly as sum over SETUPs of pi(x)*net(x). The only statistical problem is generalisation from a few thousand contexts, so the right tools are cost-sensitive policy learning (value-maximising policy trees, cost-proportionate weighting) and honest selection, not bandit exploration. (2) Sequential RL is genuinely justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable: the in-trade exit (hold/exit/partial each bar; 1m IS has ~186k intraday bar-steps inside positions, ~800k once trajectories are extended to the 15:25 square-off) and, at session level, whether to keep trading today. On a price-taker's tape the dynamics are exogenous (an Exo-MDP): any exit policy can be replayed exactly and the hindsight-optimal exit is computable per trade, so OPE (DR/MAGIC) is not the bottleneck; generalisation and multiplicity are. Deep offline RL (CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer) and neural generators (TimeGAN, diffusion) are not runnable here (no torch) and would be badly over-parameterised for 4.5k trajectories anyway; the studies say so and use the closest feasible analogues (pessimistic tree-ensemble FQI, hindsight-imitation, GMM-Markov and session-bootstrap tapes). (3) Sizing is a downstream Kelly problem that only exists once a positive-conditional-edge region is found; the raw book (win rate 15%, mean -922 INR) has negative Kelly, and the study is written to return "0 lots" honestly. (4) Costs are 1,050-1,120 INR per trade and the median 1m trade moves 9 pts, so a gate that trades less always raises net by the saved costs: every study judges on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, the session-matched random control at the same per-session position count (fz_report.random_control), the permutation p, and (new here) the multiplicity-adjusted SPA/PBO from session-block resampling. (5) Leakage discipline is shared: features from the as-of columns only (prefixes fnd_, fwd_, fzpos_, st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones/visits final-state fields are excluded), contiguous session-block CV with purge (drop training trades whose exit falls in the test block) and a 2-session embargo, OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) touched once per study at the end; the 5-minute engine trades are re-cut at 15:25 from bars because the build carries no square-off (358 of 1,012 held overnight). Priority order: the gate (1), the exit policy (2), then the robustness/multiplicity certificate that must pass before any key ships (3), the certified operating point (4), sizing (5), the session-stop rule (6). Compute: every study fits in one process under 1 GB; the two heavy jobs (1m FQI ensemble, 1m synthetic tapes) must not run concurrently with each other because each peaks near 900 MB.

60	## Studies

194	### quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo (priority 1)
195	
196	**technique.** Validation harness: purged k-fold with embargo keyed on label end time, Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (CPCV) backtest paths, CSCV probability of backtest overfitting (PBO), deflated Sharpe ratio, minimum backtest length, stationary block bootstrap of sessions, and a shared trials ledger for every candidate gate from H1-H5 and these studies.
197	
198	**what_it_answers.** Are the in-sample improvements of any candidate gate (rooms ST7/ST8, H2 regime, H3 volume, H4 levels, H5 rule lists, the studies below) larger than what picking the best of N trials produces by chance on 823 (5m) or a few thousand (1m) SETUPs? Which candidates have earned the single out-of-sample look? How many candidates can this sample afford before selection bias dominates?
199	
200	**method.** (1) Splitter module in the scratchpad, importable by every study: groups = 12 contiguous session blocks on IS (about 85 sessions each); purge = drop training SETUPs whose label lifetime [setup_i, label_exit_i] intersects the test block's bar range (label_exit_i = the label's own exit bar: the 15:25 bar for the intraday label, fnd_exit_i for the engine label which runs to 70 sessions on 5m and would purge a lot, one more reason to train on the intraday label); embargo = 3 sessions after each test block (longest feature memory: room age 3 sessions on 5m, vol_med60, range36, BSADF window 1 session). Exposes split(X, y, groups) so sklearn cross_val_predict and CalibratedClassifierCV(cv=iterable) accept it. (2) CPCV with N = 12 groups, k = 2 test groups: 66 purged train/test splits assembled into 11 full backtest paths per model; each study reports the distribution over paths (median, 5th percentile) of its kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference, control percentile and winner recall, not one number. (3) Trials ledger (CSV, append-only): one row per candidate configuration any study or H1-H5 evaluates, including every threshold a greedy search tries: candidate id, config JSON, label used, per-session IS net vector of the kept book, n_kept, script sha. (4) CSCV / PBO: matrix M candidates x T = 1,026 IS sessions of kept net per session; S = 16 blocks, all C(16,8) = 12,870 IS/OOS partitions; per partition the IS-best candidate (by mean kept net per session and, separately, by the kept-vs-skipped statistic) and its relative OOS rank; PBO = share of partitions with logit(rank) < 0; also the IS-vs-OOS performance degradation slope. (5) Deflated Sharpe ratio for each finalist: per-session Sharpe of the kept book, deflated by the expected maximum Sharpe under M trials (variance of Sharpe across the ledger), with skew and kurtosis of per-session net; p-value reported. (6) Minimum backtest length for the observed Sharpe and M, checked against T. (7) Stationary block bootstrap of sessions (Politis-Romano, mean block 10 sessions, 2,000 draws, seeded) for confidence intervals of kept-vs-skipped differences and control percentiles; this is the harness's only generative component. (8) Pre-registered go/no-go: a candidate goes to OOS only if PBO <= 0.2, the CPCV 5th-percentile kept-vs-skipped difference > 0 and DSR p < 0.1; at most three candidates across all lenses (one rule list, one model-based threshold, plus the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator) are scored on OOS, by a separate script that reads frozen JSON. Outputs: the splitter, the ledger, a PBO/DSR table per timeframe, the go/no-go list.
201	
202	**leakage_controls.** The harness is the control for the other studies: purging by label end time removes train/test overlap of label lifetimes (holds past the entry session exist: 358 of 1,003 engine trades on 5m); the 3-session embargo covers feature memory; the ledger makes every trial visible so PBO counts them; the harness consumes IS per-session vectors only and never opens an OOS row; the OOS evaluator is a separate script reading frozen candidate JSON plus sha, run once; block-bootstrap and CPCV draws are seeded like fz_report.random_control so every number reproduces.
203	
204	**compute.** CPCV: 66 splits x 3 models per study that uses it, about 200 fits on <= 5k rows x 100 features, 10-15 CPU-minutes per timeframe; CSCV: precompute 16 block sums per candidate, then 12,870 partitions x M x 8 additions in numpy, seconds for M <= 2,000 (matrix 2,000 x 1,026 float64 = 16 MB); bootstrap 2,000 draws vectorised, under 1 minute; peak memory under 300 MB, one process.
205	
206	**libraries.** numpy, pandas, scipy.stats (skew, kurtosis, norm), itertools.combinations, joblib for caching; fz_report.random_control and permutation_p imported read-only as reference implementations; no new installs.
207	
208	**output_as_config.** Not trading numbers but provenance every ST13/ST14 file must carry: "validation": {"scheme": "purged_kfold_embargo", "blocks": 12, "embargo_sessions": 3, "cpcv_paths": 11, "label": "foundation_intraday_1525", "trials": M, "pbo": x, "dsr_p": y, "ledger_sha": ...} inside the strategy file's provenance object, plus the go/no-go table naming which candidates were allowed to touch OOS. The lab's existing random_control / permutation_p stay the headline statistics.
209	
210	**novelty.** Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning (2018) ch. 7 (purged k-fold, embargo), ch. 11-12 (backtest dangers, CPCV), ch. 14 (backtest statistics); Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado and Zhu (2017) The probability of backtest overfitting, J. Computational Finance (CSCV/PBO); Bailey and Lopez de Prado (2014) The Deflated Sharpe Ratio, J. Portfolio Management; Harvey and Liu (2015) multiple-testing haircuts; Politis and Romano (1994) stationary bootstrap. Current because PBO/DSR with a trials ledger is what the 2020s quant-ML literature demands before an OOS claim, and the brief's H5 greedy threshold searches are exactly the multiplicity it measures.
211	
212	**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: Trap: the ledger only counts trials that are logged, PBO/DSR over M threshold sweeps of one feature over-count independent trials while unlogged looks (dashboard, LLM summaries, the ST9-12 exit grid already run on 2026) under-count them, and the CSCV matrix on T = 1,026 sessions includes 447 IS sessions with no SETUP whose zero rows are identical across candidates and inflate per-session Sharpe. Fix: make the harness the only evaluator (evaluate(candidate) appends to the ledger as a side effect; no other code path may return a kept-vs-skipped number); report an effective trial count from the candidate-correlation matrix next to M; build CSCV/DSR/bootstrap on active sessions only (579 on 1m); merge study 15's SPA, adversarial drift and 5m null tapes into this harness so there is one bootstrap and one PBO; re-price every comparator (raw Foundation, frozen ST7/ST8) on the same L1 15:25 label the candidates use; stamp every OOS table with 'OOS window = published lab window and already used by the ST9-12 exit grid'.
213	
214	**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 5 · expected value 4 · keep True — fix: Make this THE single harness: merge decision-making-3's (a)/(b) into it (one splitter = 12 contiguous IS session blocks, purge by the label's own exit bar, 3-session embargo; one append-only ledger; one PBO threshold 0.2, not 0.5). Expose score(candidate_json, label='L1') as the only way any study obtains a kept-vs-skipped number, so the ledger cannot be bypassed. Add the kept-n floors from decision-making-1 (kept share >= 20%, kept n >= 300 on 1m / 80 on 5m) to the go/no-go so a tiny lucky subset cannot win the kept-vs-skipped statistic. Per-session Sharpe/DSR must use only sessions with a SETUP (579 of 1,026 IS sessions on 1m; the rest are structural zeros). The OOS evaluator is one script, run once, for at most 3 frozen candidates across all 18 studies; every other study's 'OOS once' clause is struck and replaced by 'submit to the harness'. Compute is minutes; peak < 300 MB is fine on the 759 MB currently free.

import os, sys, json
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True

sys.path.insert(0, OUT)
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import harness as H
ST = os.path.join(OUT, "studies", "h1_gate_audit")
F = json.load(open(os.path.join(ST, "findings.json")))
S = json.load(open(os.path.join(ST, "h1_summary.json")))

print("== script sha vs ledger ==")
print("h1_gate_audit.py", H.file_sha(os.path.join(ST, "h1_gate_audit.py")), "(ledger 1684715a158b4ff4)")
print("h1_posthoc.py   ", H.file_sha(os.path.join(ST, "h1_posthoc.py")), "(ledger 191b2aa2ee4997f4)")
print("ledger sha now  ", H.ledger_sha(), "(findings: audit 33170f8df9f5d50e, posthoc 1ee15dc04860b284; later studies appended since)")

led = {r["id"]: r for r in H.read_ledger("h1")}

def txt(s): return s.astype(object).where(s.notna(), "none").astype(str)

for tf in ("minute", "5minute"):
    for label in ("L1", "L0"):
        T = H.load(tf, label)
        rows = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
        Fis = T.F[T.is_mask]
        kept = T.F.fz_traded.astype(bool).to_numpy()
        fj = F["timeframes"][tf][label]
        print(f"\n===== {tf}/{label}: IS n {len(rows)} (findings {fj['n_is']}), OOS n {int(T.oos_mask.sum())}")
        # as-of status of the columns used to build variants / keys
        asof = set(T.asof_columns())
        print(" as-of? fz_gate", "fz_gate" in asof, "| fz_block_reason", "fz_block_reason" in asof, "| fzpost_outcome_gate", "fzpost_outcome_gate" in asof, "| fz_traded", "fz_traded" in asof)
        # frozen metrics reproduced without the ledger (controls off: no randomness needed for these)
        m = H.metrics(T, kept, rows, "refute", controls=False)
        fz = fj["frozen"]
        chk = {k: (m[k], fz[k]) for k in ("kept_mean", "skipped_mean", "diff", "loser_recall", "loser_precision", "winner_recall_weighted", "top_decile_winners_skipped", "kept_pf", "sign_blocks") if k in fz}
        bad = {k: v for k, v in chk.items() if v[0] is None or abs(float(v[0]) - float(v[1])) > 0.011}
        print(" frozen metrics reproduce:", "OK" if not bad else f"MISMATCH {bad}", "| kept_n", m["kept_n"], fz.get("kept_n", fj.get("kept_n")))
        base_loser = float((~T.win[T.is_mask]).mean())
        print(f" base loser rate {base_loser:.4f} (findings {fj['base_loser_rate']}), lift {m['loser_precision']/base_loser:.3f} (findings {fz['lift']}); skip share {1-m['kept_share']:.4f} vs loser recall {m['loser_recall']}")
